column3: MT 8:23. NKJV reads “the latter” as “more heavily oppressed her,” taking the verb הִכְבִּיד (“make heavy/honored”) negatively, and renders “nations” “Gentiles.”
MT 9:1. Close to the Hebrew; בְּאֶרֶץ צַלְמָוֶת (“deep darkness”) is rendered “the shadow of death.”
MT 9:2. NKJV follows the Qere “its joy” instead of the Kethiv “not” (“you did not increase the joy”), and renders the verbs as past.
MT 9:3. Close to the Hebrew.
MT 9:4. Close to the Hebrew; כָל־ סְאוֹן (“every boot”) is rendered “every warrior’s sandal,” and “with shaking” “from the noisy battle.”
MT 9:5. NKJV capitalizes “Child” and “Son” messianically; “Wonder, Counselor” is rendered as two titles, and “Father of perpetuity” “Everlasting Father.”
MT 9:6. Close to the Hebrew; “to establish it and to sustain it” is rendered “To order it and establish it,” and “in justice and righteousness” “with judgment and justice.”
MT 9:7. Close to the Hebrew; “the Lord” (Adonai) is rendered “The LORD.”
MT 9:8. Close to the Hebrew.
MT 9:9. Close to the Hebrew.
MT 9:10. Close to the Hebrew; “he provoked” is rendered “spur… on.”
MT 9:11. Close to the Hebrew; “Aram from the east… from the west” is rendered “The Syrians before and the Philistines behind.”
MT 9:12. Close to the Hebrew.
MT 9:13. Close to the Hebrew.
MT 9:14. Close to the Hebrew.
MT 9:15. Close to the Hebrew; “confused” is rendered “destroyed.”
MT 9:16. Close to the Hebrew; “the Lord” (Adonai) is rendered “the LORD,” and חָנֵף (“godless”) “a hypocrite.”
MT 9:17. Close to the Hebrew; “they have swirled” is rendered “They shall mount up.”
MT 9:18. Close to the Hebrew.
MT 9:19. Close to the Hebrew; “devoured” is rendered “snatch.”
MT 9:20. Close to the Hebrew; NKJV supplies “shall devour” and “shall be.”
